title: A Quaker meeting
hookLine: no minister, no music, only silence and occasional words

lines: BENCHES IN A SQUARE, FACING IN.
NO PULPIT, NO ALTAR, NO ORGAN.
cards: Benches set in a square, facing each other. No pulpit, no altar, no organ. Maybe a small table in the middle with flowers and a Bible.
People come in quietly and sit down, and then nothing happens, for a long time. A clock ticks. Someone shifts on the bench.

Twenty people, sitting still, saying nothing, together. Then, maybe halfway through, an older man stands up, says three sentences about his granddaughter and a verse he can't stop thinking about, and sits down again.
The silence closes back over. This is worship too.

teach.h: NO PLAN: ANYONE MAY BE GIVEN WORDS.
teach.b: Quakers call themselves the Religious Society of Friends, and their worship a meeting. In the form described here, called unprogrammed, there's no minister and no plan.
Friends speak of something of God in everyone, so anyone in the room may be the one given words to say. Some weeks a few people speak; some weeks nobody does. First, the waiting.
Friends aren't trying to empty their minds; they're listening. A psalm puts it plainly: "Be still, and know that I am God." Second, the voice.
When Elijah hides in a cave, God tells him to stand on the mountain.

teach.h: NOT THE WIND: A STILL SMALL VOICE.
teach.b: "But the LORD was not in the wind: and after the wind an earthquake; but the LORD was not in the earthquake: And after the earthquake a fire; but the LORD was not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice."
Not the loud things. The small one, after. Friends wait for that.
If someone feels truly moved, they stand, speak briefly, and sit. That's called ministry. Others don't answer or argue; they let the words settle into the quiet.
Sometimes, Friends say, the silence changes. It stops being twenty people sitting alone and becomes one people listening together: a gathered meeting.
Jesus said, "For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them." Not every Quaker church works this way; some Friends' churches have pastors, hymns and sermons.
But in the silent meeting, the gift is a stillness shared.

how: In an unprogrammed Quaker meeting for worship, Friends sit together in silence, and anyone who feels moved may stand and speak briefly; other Friends' churches hold programmed worship with pastors, hymns and sermons.

games.q: you're Elijah, standing on the mountain. a wind tears at the rocks, then an earthquake, then a fire. where is the LORD?
o: in the still small voice, after them all.
games.why: "the LORD was not in the wind … not in the earthquake … not in the fire: and after the fire a still small voice."

practice: If someone's near you, ask if they'll sit quietly with you for two minutes; if you're alone, remember that other people somewhere are sitting in silence right now, and sit with them that way.
Don't fill the quiet; if a sentence rises that feels worth keeping, notice it and let it rest. If you pray, you can wait for the still small voice.
